name: GridFeed Night Stand Vendor Full Kit
description:
The GridFeed night cart vendor kit is a layered, weather-adapted street food uniform assembled from a mix of GridFeed franchise-issued pieces and personal additions. The base is a long-sleeve henley in deep burgundy with a GridFeed logo heat-transfer on the left chest — a stylized bowl over a power grid node. Over it goes the GridFeed-issued bistro apron: heavy-duty waxed canvas in charcoal with wide front pockets, a hanging towel loop, and a reinforced bib panel that deflects steam and hot grease. The apron strings wrap twice around the waist and tie at the front for quick removal. A sweat-resistant skull cap in matching charcoal keeps hair contained and is covered during wet weather by a wide-brim waterproof overhatch that clips to the cap's brim rail.

Lower body is the vendor's own choice: Goretek WorkHold tape-reinforced trousers in dark navy, worn with a canvas-weave belt and a phone-and-fob loop clipped at the left hip. The trousers have been hem-adjusted for the vendor's digitigrade geneware legs — the inner seam has been let out and the calf panels expanded with a contrasting charcoal panel by a Circuit-tier tailor, accommodating the reverse-joint structure cleanly. Footwear is the Foundry Broadfoot Work Sneaker in matte black — grippy, easy to clean, rated for eight-hour standing. The right forearm carries a thin chrome payment-reader interface mount, a common aug-addition for vendors who process Φ transactions without reaching for a terminal. The whole kit smells like five-spice and rain.
functionality: Grease and steam-resistant waxed apron with deep storage pockets, moisture-resistant skull cap and clip-on overhatch for rain, digitigrade gene-compatible trouser modification, chrome payment reader arm mount for fast Φ transactions, easy-clean footwear for long standing shifts
what_it_says: Someone running their own corner of the economy — small, independent-ish (franchise-affiliated, not owned), out in all weather, feeding people. The geneware trouser mod says they spent money on tailoring rather than buying new, which is a Circuit-tier calculation. The chrome payment mount says they move volume and move it fast. The apron strings tied at the front say they have done this enough that they do not think about it.
worn_by: Circuit-tier vendor workers with geneware modifications
manufacturer: GridFeed Franchise Supply (apron, logo henley, cap); Goretek (trousers); Foundry (footwear); independent tailor (trouser modification)
price_range: Φ 160–Φ 240 (franchise-issued pieces at cost; personal items self-purchased)
story_hooks: The vendor's payment reader has been skimming a fraction of a Φ from each transaction for months, routing it to an account they did not set up — and the GridFeed franchise auditor arrives tomorrow.
A character who needs to disappear for a few hours takes a shift at the cart — but the regular vendor's regulars know something is wrong immediately.
The cart's location at the corner of two transit corridors makes it the perfect dead-drop point; the vendor has been passing packages without knowing what is in them.
related_entities: Ouroboros Energy Power Distribution Trunk Network

physical_description.visual_profile: A street-hardened night vendor's layered utility uniform that reads as working-class functional with personal adaptation. The silhouette is compact and mobile — nothing loose or flowing — with visible augmentation integration. The burgundy henley peeks from under the charcoal apron creating a subtle color contrast. The modified trousers accommodate non-standard leg geometry, signaling both cybernetic enhancement and resourceful tailoring. The overall impression is someone built for 8-hour shifts in tight quarters, processing transactions and handling hot food without stopping.
physical_description.fit: Tailored for movement and accessibility — the henley is fitted through the torso but not restrictive, the apron sits high at the waist with deep front pockets positioned for easy reach, trousers are straight-cut with intentional calf expansion to accommodate digitigrade geneware. The cap sits snug, the overhatch clips securely. Everything designed for rapid removal or adjustment mid-shift.
physical_description.primary_material: Heat-transfer printed henley (synthetic blend), heavy-duty waxed canvas apron, tape-reinforced Goretek work trousers (ballistic weave), matte-finish Foundry work sneakers (reinforced synthetic/rubber composite), charcoal cotton-weave skull cap with waterproof overhatch
physical_description.texture: Waxed canvas is stiff and water-resistant with a subtle sheen; the henley is soft cotton-poly blend with slight pilling from repeated washing; trousers show tight, sturdy weave with visible reinforcement tape at stress points; sneakers have deep tread and grippy sole; the contrasting calf panel is raw charcoal canvas, slightly rougher than the main trouser material
physical_description.color_scheme: Deep burgundy henley with metallic heat-transfer logo, charcoal waxed canvas apron, dark navy trousers with charcoal panel inserts, matte black sneakers, matching charcoal skull cap. The chrome payment-reader interface on the right forearm provides an accent of clinical silver.
physical_description.closures: Apron ties wrap twice around waist and knot at front for quick removal; trousers use standard snap fly; cap has internal elastic and brim clips for the overhatch; sneakers are lace-less slip-on design with friction-fit heel; belt is canvas with friction-lock buckle
distinctive_features: GridFeed logo heat-transfer on left chest — stylized bowl over power grid node
Waxed canvas apron with wide front pockets and hanging towel loop
Reinforced bib panel deflecting steam and hot grease
Custom tailor-modified trousers with let-out inner seams and contrasting charcoal calf panels for digitigrade geneware accommodation
Charcoal skull cap with detachable waterproof overhatch and clip-rail system
Chrome payment-reader interface mount on right forearm
Phone-and-fob loop clipped at left hip
Matte black Broadfoot sneakers with 8-hour standing rating
Evidence of heavy use — slight grease staining on apron bib, faint scuff marks on trousers and footwear
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3-4 working class. The GridFeed franchise issues standard pieces (apron, henley, cap) that are durable but not luxury; the personal additions (Goretek trousers, Foundry footwear, independent tailoring) show self-investment in quality tools for a demanding job. The chrome augmentation interface is functional, not decorative.
physical_description.cultural_context: Street vendor, night-shift food service, augmented working class. Wearing this outfit signals you're part of the informal economy, physically adapted for non-standard work, and comfortable with geneware modifications. The GridFeed branding marks you as franchised labor — a step above completely independent but still sub-tier-2. The custom tailoring indicates you've been in this role long enough to invest in proper adaptation.
physical_description.condition_typical: Broken-in and working-worn. The apron shows faint grease staining around the bib and pocket edges; the trousers have creasing at the knees and cuffs from repeated eight-hour shifts; the sneakers are scuffed at the toes and sides but kept clean; the henley may have small, nearly-invisible bleach spots from steam exposure; the cap's sweatband is slightly darkened. Everything is functional and maintained, not pristine, but clearly cared-for within the constraints of street-work reality.

image_prompt: A cyberpunk street vendor in full GridFeed night cart uniform photographed against a rain-slick alley backdrop, neon signs reflecting off wet pavement. Focus on the burgundy henley and charcoal waxed-canvas apron with visible logo heat-transfer, the custom-modified trousers showing charcoal calf panels accommodating digitigrade geometry, matte black Foundry sneakers planted firmly on wet concrete. The right forearm catches moody blue-amber light on the chrome payment-reader interface mount. The charcoal skull cap sits low, the detachable waterproof overhatch clipped to the brim. A faint aura of steam and five-spice lingers. Shot with moody street photography lighting, cool tones dominating, the subject framed as a hardworking augmented figure embedded in the GLMZ night economy.
